column1: # Per-component decomposition groups: NAME <TAB> REGEX
# One regex per logical component, matched against the symbol names in BOTH
# profiles, and the SELF costs summed. Rows are tried IN ORDER and the first match
# wins, so a narrow row must precede the wider one that would otherwise swallow it
# -- `nnue acc apply` before `nnue other`.
# WHAT A ROW MEANS. "This much of the work happens here." It is a claim about COST,
# not about the algorithm; tools/fingerprint_groups.tsv owns the call-count claim,
# which is immune to inlining at the callee but not at the caller -- a function
# inlined into its caller leaves the profile entirely.
# CHOOSE SYMBOLS THAT SURVIVE INLINING ON BOTH SIDES. A row matching nothing on
# either side is reported BY NAME rather than printed as a zero, because a zero
# reads as a total win forever and the real cause is usually a symbol that stopped
# surviving LTO. mcfish builds with LTO, so the specialised search bodies appear as
# `search_node_nonpv'2` and similar clones -- the regexes below are deliberately
# loose enough to keep collecting them when the clone suffix changes.
# STARTUP IS ITS OWN ROWS, and that is not bookkeeping. At a small depth the net
# parse and the magic-table init are the LARGEST rows in the profile -- 17.6% and
# 14.4% of a depth-7 run -- so a table that folded them into a total would report a
# search ratio that is mostly startup. Read `search total` and the NNUE rows against
# each other; read the startup rows to know whether the depth was big enough that
# they stopped mattering.
# ---- startup: everything before the first node ----------------------------------
net parse
magics init
history clear
nnue acc apply
nnue refresh
nnue affine
nnue eval
nnue other
search nodes
iterative deepening
movepick
history update
do/undo move
threats
check info
legality
movegen
# NO `tt` ROW, and its absence is a measurement rather than an oversight: clang
# inlines tt_probe and tt_save into the search at every tier this tree builds, so
# they carry no self cost and a row for them matched nothing. Their work is inside
# `search nodes`. Add the row back only if a profile ever shows the symbols.
# ---- tablebases: absent from the bench list, present under a probing workload ----
# Both rows report "matched nothing" on a bench-list run, and that is CORRECT: every
# bench position has more men on it than any table tb-fetch installs. Drive the tool
# with a probing workload (tools/cases/tb_probe.fens, plus a SyzygyPath setoption
# line) to make them appear.
tb decode
tb probe
# ---- libc: not ours, but it is real cost and it must not vanish into the gap -----
libc mem
